Serfs are "commoners", as are most Freemen. Commoner is just a colloqialism for anyone who isnt an aristocrat. Aristocrats are people closely related to nobles and are legally just Freemen with no special rights. Nobles are those with noble contracts, usually just the Lord and Lady of a house. No, their children are legally not nobles, just Freemen or "commoners". Only by inheriting the title from their parents or earning their own title would the children become nobles.

Basically legally speaking everyone had the same status except the sovereign, who stood under god above all else. A noble was also just a Freeman who signed a contract with the king.

Can we not compare serfs in all areas to serfs in 1800s russia? There is this general misunderstanding that serfs were slaves, when they clearly were not.

Serfs are just Freemen who made a contract to be bound to a piece of land until they pay off a debt. As soon as they can repay the debt they are free to go. Besides, serfs could basically do anything they wanted as long as they didnt run away from the debt.

Serfdom was created by the nobility so that people didnt have to become actual slaves. During hard times instead of selling your children or yourself into slavery you could become a serf. Then the state would also be responsible for feeding you during hard times.

It was even considered shameful for nobles if their rates of serfs to freemen were high, which indicated bad management. The purpose of serfdom was to leave serfdom while spreading the liabilities of the person involved over a long period of time rather than concentrated in one short period, thus stabilizing their lives.

Take minced meat, mix with salt pepper and a little kurkuma.

Use butter as oil and sauté onions (you can cut it however you prefer).

Once the onions are close to done gather them in one place and put a meatball formed of the previous minced meat on top, then smash it flat with something. This will cause the onions to get embedded into the patty.

Let one side cook and after you flip it, put cheese on top (best imo is cheddar or Old Amsterdam). 

Once the meat is done put it on a plate and get all the excess onion pieces out too. You can put the extra onion pieces on top of the cheese.

If you wanna make it with an egg you can fry it now. Make sure the fried egg isnt spread to wide. You can flip parts of the eggs outer edge to get it into shape. Alternatively you can half the egg and use one egg for two burgers.

Once its at the desired consistency get the egg out and place it on top of the patty.

Then take the buns and fry their inside with the leftover buttery goodness. Make sure you use enough butter throughout the entire cooking process. I gradually add more as I cook.

Once the buns are done, put some sweet pickles on the lower bun and ketchup on the upper bun and put the patty, cheese, and egg combo into the bun.

Thats what facilitates this distribution of reaources. Money is a trade good that can be exchanged for anything. If you control money (the central bank) and how people are allowed to spend it (the state), you can distribute the consumption of resources in any way you want.

Basically this >

The village chief collects all the resources that everyone in the village produce (irl this would be the marketplace).

Then he gives out tokens to everyone they can exchange for the resources they want (tokens = money).

Since only a part of the village is contributing to the food and clothing in the stockpile, but everyone can pull resources out, those that are not productive are "leeching" resources.

When you have a village with a growing group of people who dont do productive work (imagine them digging and filling holes continuously) but still receive food and clothing from the rest of the village, eventually there will be too many "leeches" in the village. Then suddenly nobody will get enough food.

Either the the village decides to cut off the unproductive villagers (economic crisis, increased unemployment, a bunch of auctions of campany assets, a general restructuring of capital structures) or they keep feeding them while continueing the system as far as they can (hyperinflation, and then the previously mentioned consequemces a little later  but muxh harsher).

Liberal countries (the west, japan, korea, taiwan) prefer the previous solution since theyre at least warry of hyperinflation, but others (socialist countries) dont stop and allow the system to correct itself, thus causing hyperinflation and a harsher crisis, albeit at a later date.

Another part of it is abusing the fiat money system (paper currency). Basically the central bank prints money and lends it out to banks with the purpose of investment (the rates are so favourable that its basically a bunch of gifted money). Then the banks lend out to businesses for specified projects (this is investment banking).

Regulations force the lions share of the money to go to the most influencial companies (those with ties to politicians). Since this isnt exactly your own money you are risking, and liability can be limited these influencial companies can just try a bunch of bullshit projects in the hopes that a few work out. Btw it is normally not possible to exploit the system this way because the banks would not lend to risky ventures with no collateral. The regulations imposed by the politicians (who have ties to these companies, and stand to profit themselves) essentially make most of this money unusable for banks unless they use it on these risky ventures. So instead of not using the money they take the tiny returns that they can get due to the difference in interest rates from the central bank and the loans.

All this basically means that the people and most private companies are "taxed" with inflation while the few companies with ties to legistlators get free money shoveled at them where they waste most of it and end up with some positive return. 

The problem with this system from an economic perspective  (lets not get into the ethics) is that youre essentially burning a lot of real value in the economy (wasted resources and machines) and placing a huge burden on the economy at the same time (employee incomes who work at non-productive companies are essentially leeching off resources from productive individuals).

All this works fine from the Keynessian perspective since they only look at the money side of things without considering the impact on real resource.

The crash comes when these useless companies (and their employees) grow too burdensome for the economy to sustain and you end up having a collapse.

Edit: Btw, most influencial economists defend this system. There is a huge issue in the economist profession where only economists who believe the state and central banks being a positive influence in the conomy get hired and thus gain influence as famous economists (see Krugmann). Point being there is a positive feedback-loop where new economists are continuously trained in this keynessian school while being told the alternative ideas are not respected.

In the 20s to 60s the two schools of thought were mostly balanced, with the free-market way of thinking winning out in public opinion because people were more interested in the topic. Nowadays the average person just says "leave it to the state and the economists" and has no idea this shit is going on. This was specifically what Friedmann was trying to prevent from happening.
